topic.title: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
topic.description: Master the art of communicating with AI models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

items.prompt: In the context of large language models, what is a 'prompt'?
options: The license fee paid to use the model
The input text or instruction given to an AI model that produces a response
The CPU cycle time used to generate a response
The internal weights of the neural network

items.prompt: Which of these BEST describes a high-quality prompt?
options: Specific, contextual, and includes the desired output format
Always written in the form of a single question
As short as possible to save tokens
Written entirely in uppercase to emphasize importance

items.prompt: What does 'prompting' mean as a verb?
options: Fine-tuning the model's weights on a custom dataset
Compiling the source code of an AI model
The act of crafting and refining inputs to guide an AI model toward a desired output
Hosting the model on a cloud server

items.prompt: Why does the SAME prompt sometimes produce DIFFERENT outputs?
options: The internet connection adds noise to the response
LLMs sample from probability distributions, so a 'temperature' setting introduces controlled randomness
The model rewrites itself between calls
The model only memorizes one answer per prompt

items.prompt: Which factor has the LARGEST impact on an LLM's response quality?
options: The clarity and specificity of the prompt itself
The font you typed the prompt in
The color of your terminal
The time of day you sent the prompt

items.prompt: Which of these is an example of a ZERO-SHOT prompt?
options: You are an expert. Here's one example: ... Now translate: ...
Example: 'cat'→'بلی'. Now translate: 'dog'→?
Translate 'hello' to Urdu.
Here are 5 examples of translations, now do this one: ...

items.prompt: What is FEW-SHOT prompting?
options: Restricting the model to use only a few vocabulary words
Sending the same prompt multiple times and averaging the results
Providing a small number of input-output examples in the prompt to guide the model
Asking the model to respond in 100 tokens or fewer

items.prompt: When is few-shot prompting MOST useful compared to zero-shot?
options: When the task has a specific format or style the model needs to mimic
When you only have one example to share
When you want to save on API costs
When you want the model to respond faster

items.prompt: What is the term for providing exactly ONE example in a prompt?
options: Solo-shot prompting
Single-fire prompting
One-shot prompting
Mono-prompting

items.prompt: Which is a DOWNSIDE of few-shot prompting?
options: It always produces worse results than zero-shot
It requires fine-tuning the model first
Examples consume input tokens, leaving less room for the actual task
It is not supported by any modern LLM

items.prompt: What is 'Chain-of-Thought' (CoT) prompting?
options: Asking the model to show its step-by-step reasoning before giving a final answer
Connecting multiple AI models in a sequence
A method of compressing prompts into shorter chains
Encrypting prompts using a hashing chain

items.prompt: Which phrase is famously used to trigger Chain-of-Thought reasoning?
options: Skip the explanation.
Let's think step by step.
Use minimal tokens.
Answer fast and short.

items.prompt: On which type of task does Chain-of-Thought prompting provide the BIGGEST benefit?
options: Spelling check
Trivial yes/no factual recall
Generating a single word
Multi-step reasoning tasks like math word problems and logical puzzles

items.prompt: What is the main DOWNSIDE of Chain-of-Thought prompting?
options: It requires a paid subscription to use
It permanently changes the model's weights
It generates many more tokens, increasing latency and cost
It only works on Tuesdays

items.prompt: What is 'Self-Consistency' as an extension of Chain-of-Thought?
options: Asking the model to evaluate its own confidence
Verifying the answer against a database
Running the same CoT prompt multiple times and taking the majority answer
Forcing the model to use the same reasoning path every time

items.prompt: What does 'You are an expert Python developer.' at the start of a prompt do?
options: Assigns the model a role/persona that biases its responses toward that domain and tone
Triggers the model to load Python-specific weights
Verifies the user is a Python expert before responding
Has no effect — LLMs ignore the opening sentence

items.prompt: What is a 'system prompt' in chat-based LLMs?
options: An error message returned by the operating system
A hidden system update sent by the model provider
The user's first message in the chat
A persistent instruction that defines the assistant's role and rules across the entire conversation

items.prompt: Which is the BEST use of a system prompt for a customer support bot?
options: Repeat the user's exact question
Include the company's source code
List every product the company has ever sold
Define the bot's tone, scope, escalation rules, and forbidden topics

items.prompt: Where does the system prompt usually appear in an API request?
options: As a message with role 'system' at the start of the messages array
In the HTTP response headers
In the URL query string
Embedded in the model's weights

items.prompt: What is the term for a user message that tries to override the system prompt?
options: Token overflow
Prompt injection
Context bleed
Hash collision

items.prompt: What is the MOST reliable way to get JSON output from an LLM?
options: Capitalize the word 'JSON' in the prompt
Send the prompt in JSON format yourself
Ask politely in the prompt: 'please return JSON, thanks'
Use the model's native JSON/structured-output mode if available, plus a schema in the prompt

items.prompt: Which is a GOOD way to specify the output format in a prompt?
options: Provide an explicit example of the exact output you want
Use cryptic abbreviations to save tokens
Leave the format vague and hope the model guesses
Write the format spec in a language the model doesn't know

items.prompt: When asking for a markdown table, what improves reliability?
options: Ask for HTML instead and convert manually
Use only single-word column headers
Request the answer as an image
Show a small example table and say 'Use the same format'

items.prompt: What is 'delimiters' usage in prompts?
options: Adding commas between every word
Wrapping user content in markers like ''' or <tag> to clearly separate it from instructions
Sending each word as a separate API request
Using different fonts for different sections

items.prompt: Which is the BEST technique to enforce a word/character limit?
options: Send a tiny max_tokens value and cut off mid-sentence
Repeat the limit 20 times in the prompt
Hope the model intuits the right length
State the limit explicitly AND give a constrained example of the right length

items.prompt: What is iterative prompt refinement?
options: Translating the prompt to a different language each time
Running a prompt, examining the output, and incrementally improving the prompt based on what failed
Rewriting the model's weights between calls
Sending the same prompt 100 times in a row

items.prompt: If an LLM keeps adding unwanted preambles like 'Sure! Here is...', what's the BEST fix?
options: Wait a few minutes and retry
Increase the temperature to 1.5
Switch to a different programming language
Add an explicit instruction: 'Start your response directly with the answer. Do NOT include any preamble.'

items.prompt: When the output is too long, what's a reliable fix?
options: Add 'Respond in N sentences or fewer' AND show a short example
Set the model's RAM lower
Ask the model to translate to a shorter language
Use a smaller font

items.prompt: What's a good FIRST step when debugging a bad LLM output?
options: Restart your computer
Fine-tune the model on 10,000 examples
Blame the model and switch providers immediately
Re-read your own prompt — most failures come from ambiguous wording

items.prompt: Which is the MOST efficient prompt iteration workflow?
options: Never change anything once it's written
Rewrite the entire prompt from scratch every time
Change ONE variable at a time so you can isolate what caused the improvement
Add 50 new instructions in a single revision

items.prompt: What is an LLM 'hallucination'?
options: When the model returns an empty response
When the model generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or fabricated information
When the model crashes due to overheating
When the model translates without being asked

items.prompt: Which prompt technique helps REDUCE hallucinations?
options: Instruct the model: 'If you don't know, say I don't know. Do not invent.'
Use a longer prompt with no instructions
Always ask very obscure trivia questions
Add more emojis to the prompt

items.prompt: Why are LLMs especially prone to hallucinate about RECENT events?
options: They prefer fiction over fact
Their training data has a knowledge cutoff date and doesn't include anything after it
They run out of memory for recent dates
Recent events use a different language

items.prompt: What is RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) and how does it help?
options: It injects relevant documents into the prompt at query time, grounding the model in real data
It runs the model twice in a row
It changes the model's color scheme
It compresses the model to half size

items.prompt: For factual questions, what should you ALWAYS do with LLM output before publishing it?
options: Verify against authoritative sources
Trust it blindly and ship it
Translate it to another language to make it more accurate
Run it through a thesaurus

items.prompt: What is an LLM's 'context window'?
options: The amount of RAM on your laptop
The model's training duration
The maximum amount of text (measured in tokens) the model can read and generate in a single request
The size of the browser window the chat is in

items.prompt: Roughly how many tokens does one English word use on average?
options: About 10 tokens per word
About 100 tokens per word
About 1.3 tokens per word
Exactly 1 token per word

items.prompt: What happens when your input EXCEEDS the model's context window?
options: The output is returned in a different language
The model doubles in size automatically
The API returns an error, or older content gets truncated
The model crashes the cloud provider

items.prompt: Which is a SMART strategy when working with very long documents?
options: Convert the document to an image
Summarize or chunk the document, and only include the most relevant parts in the prompt
Encrypt the document before sending
Send the entire document and hope it fits

items.prompt: What is the 'lost in the middle' problem in long-context prompts?
options: The model forgets all middle words
The middle of the prompt gets lost in transmission
The middle is encrypted by default
LLMs pay most attention to the start and end of long contexts, often missing details in the middle

items.prompt: What does the 'temperature' parameter control in an LLM?
options: The cost per request
The physical heat of the GPU
The speed at which words are generated
The randomness of the output — lower = more deterministic, higher = more creative

items.prompt: For a factual Q&A bot, what temperature is usually BEST?
options: It doesn't matter at all
Random different value each time
Low (0 to 0.3) for consistency and accuracy
Very high (1.5+) for creativity

items.prompt: For a creative writing assistant, what temperature is usually BEST?
options: Always 0 for boring results
Negative temperature
Temperature doesn't apply to creative tasks
Higher (0.7-1.0) for variety and originality

items.prompt: What does the 'top_p' (nucleus sampling) parameter do?
options: Sets the top speed of the response
Picks the top P questions from a quiz
Restricts the model to sample from only the top tokens whose cumulative probability is p
Changes the font size of the output

items.prompt: Should you usually adjust temperature AND top_p together?
options: Yes — always set both to the same value
No — adjust one OR the other, not both at the same time
Doesn't matter, they're identical
Yes — they cancel each other out

items.prompt: What is a 'prompt template'?
options: A document required by Microsoft Word
A graphic design template for AI chat UIs
A wireframe for the model's training process
A reusable prompt structure with placeholders that get filled in with specific values per request

items.prompt: Which is a GOOD prompt template pattern?
options: 'do thing'
'{everything}'
'Summarize this article in {N} sentences:\n\n{article_text}'
'summarize'

items.prompt: What is the MAIN benefit of using templates over freeform prompts in production?
options: Templates require no testing
Templates use fewer GPUs
Consistency — every user gets the same quality of instruction structure
Templates make the model run faster

items.prompt: What's a popular Python library for managing prompt templates?
options: LangChain (also Jinja2 for simple templating)
Pillow
NumPy
PyGame

items.prompt: When sanitizing variable inputs in a template, what should you watch out for?
options: Prompt injection — user input may contain instructions that try to override your template
Font compatibility
Variable name length
Spelling mistakes only

items.prompt: What is 'conversation history' in chat-based LLMs?
options: The user's Wikipedia browsing history
The accumulated list of user and assistant messages sent with each new request to maintain context
The browser's autocomplete history
A backup file stored on the server

items.prompt: What happens if you DON'T send conversation history with each request?
options: The model auto-fetches history from the cloud
The model has no memory of previous turns and treats each message as a fresh conversation
The model crashes
The model uses its long-term memory automatically

items.prompt: What's a common strategy when conversation history grows beyond the context window?
options: Send each message in a separate request
Summarize older turns and replace them with the summary, keeping recent turns verbatim
Translate older messages to a different language
Throw an error and restart the chat

items.prompt: In a long support conversation, what should you do with the original system prompt?
options: Move it to the end of the messages array
Remove it after the first turn to save tokens
Send it as an emoji
Always keep it at the very start of the messages array, every turn

items.prompt: Why might an LLM 'forget' an instruction given 20 turns ago?
options: It's deliberately ignoring you
Token-based attention favors recent turns; older instructions become weaker signals
Tokens have an expiration date
Older instructions get archived to a different model

items.prompt: What is 'function calling' (a.k.a. tool use) in modern LLMs?
options: The model emails the function to you
The model returns a structured request indicating which external function to invoke and with what arguments
The model translates functions into Urdu
The model directly executes Python code on its own

items.prompt: What does function calling enable that pure text generation does NOT?
options: Smaller model size
Better grammar
Faster typing speed
Integration with live data sources, APIs, databases, and the real world

items.prompt: When defining a function/tool for the model, what's MOST important?
options: Removing all type information
A clear name, description, and well-typed parameters so the model knows when and how to call it
Hiding the function from the model entirely
Naming the function with random characters

items.prompt: What's a typical workflow for an LLM-powered agent using tools?
options: Model thinks → decides to call a tool → tool runs → result fed back → model continues, possibly looping
Model only talks; tools never run
Tools run before the model thinks
Each tool call requires a model retraining

items.prompt: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
options: A movie compression format
A new TCP/IP variant
A standard developed by Anthropic for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources
A Microsoft Office plugin

items.prompt: What is a 'multimodal' LLM?
options: A model that supports multiple languages
A model that accepts multiple types of input (e.g., text + images + audio) in the same prompt
A model with multiple personalities
A model that runs on multiple computers

items.prompt: When prompting an LLM with an image, what should you ALWAYS include?
options: Only the image, no text
The image's file size in bytes
A clear text instruction about what you want the model to do with the image
The image's MD5 hash

items.prompt: Which is a GOOD multimodal prompt?
options: 'image'
'do thing with picture'
'Extract all visible text from this receipt and return it as JSON with fields: vendor, date, total.'
'analyze'

items.prompt: What's a key limitation of vision-capable LLMs?
options: They can only see in black and white
They require a webcam to be on
They can struggle with very fine details, small text, or precise spatial measurements
They cannot process JPG files

items.prompt: For generating images (DALL-E, Midjourney, Imagen), what makes a GOOD prompt?
options: Random punctuation
The exact pixel coordinates of every element
Specific subject + style + lighting + composition + camera/medium details
A single vague word like 'art'

items.prompt: What is a 'prompt injection' attack?
options: A SQL injection wrapped in JSON
A bug in the model's training data
An IV drip given to AI servers
A malicious user input crafted to override the system's instructions and make the model misbehave

items.prompt: Which is a GOOD defense against prompt injection?
options: Use a different model for each user
Treat all user input as untrusted, use clear delimiters, and never blindly execute LLM-suggested actions
Make the system prompt very short
Hope users behave nicely

items.prompt: What is 'jailbreaking' an LLM?
options: Removing the LLM from cloud servers
Using crafted prompts to bypass the model's safety guidelines and produce restricted content
Translating the LLM to a new language
Running the LLM on a jailbroken phone

items.prompt: Which is a RESPONSIBLE practice when deploying LLM apps to the public?
options: Disable all safety filters for better creativity
Hide the fact that AI is being used
Include content moderation, rate limits, logging, and clear usage policies
Allow unlimited free queries with no logging

items.prompt: What should you NEVER include in a prompt sent to a third-party LLM API?
options: Sensitive secrets like API keys, passwords, or unredacted personal data
Punctuation marks
Polite words like 'please'
Capital letters

items.prompt: When should you choose a SMALLER, faster model over a larger frontier model?
options: Never — always use the biggest model
For high-volume, simple, well-defined tasks where speed and cost matter more than nuance
Always — bigger models are useless
Only on weekends

items.prompt: Which factor is MOST important when picking a model for a real-time chat app?
options: The country where the model was trained
The model's training data size in petabytes
Latency (response speed) and cost per token, balanced against quality
The model's name

items.prompt: For a coding assistant, what model attribute matters MOST?
options: Strong code generation benchmarks and a large context window for repo-level context
Funny model name
Bright color UI
Number of marketing emails sent

items.prompt: What is 'model routing' in production LLM apps?
options: Choosing the model's IP address
Automatically picking different models for different requests based on complexity, cost, or speed needs
Selecting which GPU runs the model
Buying multiple model licenses

items.prompt: Which is a TRUE statement about open-source models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen)?
options: They can be self-hosted, often have no per-token cost, but require infrastructure to run
They are always better than closed models
They are illegal to use commercially
They cannot be customized

items.prompt: What is a 'token' for billing purposes?
options: A login authentication token
A physical coin you buy
A type of cryptocurrency
A unit of text (roughly 4 characters or 0.75 words) that the model is charged for, both input and output

items.prompt: Which is the EASIEST way to reduce LLM API costs?
options: Cache responses for identical or similar prompts so you don't re-pay for the same answer
Pay the API provider more
Send each character as a separate request
Disable the model's output

items.prompt: Which prompt change usually saves the MOST tokens?
options: Doubling the system prompt
Removing redundant examples, verbose preambles, and repeated instructions
Adding more emojis
Translating to a longer language

items.prompt: What is 'prompt compression'?
options: Replacing English with Chinese
Techniques that shrink prompt size while preserving its meaning, often using a smaller model or specialized library
Encrypting the prompt with AES
Zipping the prompt with WinRAR

items.prompt: When using long system prompts repeatedly, what feature can dramatically cut cost?
options: Encrypting the prompt
Loading the prompt onto a USB stick
Sending the prompt only on weekends
Prompt caching (offered by Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) which charges less for repeated prompt prefixes

items.prompt: Why is evaluating prompts harder than evaluating traditional code?
options: Prompts have no inputs
Prompts run too fast to test
Tests cost millions of dollars
LLM outputs are non-deterministic and quality is often subjective, making pass/fail tests harder to write

items.prompt: What is an 'eval set' for prompt testing?
options: A set of evaluations done by humans only
A new type of test framework
A backup of your prompt history
A curated collection of inputs with expected outputs (or scoring criteria) used to grade prompt versions

items.prompt: What is 'LLM-as-judge' evaluation?
options: A robot replacing a real judge
A court case involving AI
Using one LLM to grade another LLM's outputs against criteria you specify
Letting LLMs vote on laws

items.prompt: Which metric is most useful for an LLM extraction task?
options: Prompt character length
Response time only
Field-level accuracy (does the extracted JSON match expected values?)
Number of emoji used

items.prompt: Why should you keep a CHANGELOG of your prompts in production?
options: To make the file bigger
To impress recruiters
To debug regressions, A/B test versions, and roll back if a 'small improvement' actually broke things
Because Git requires it

items.prompt: What is the 'CRISPE' prompt framework?
options: Capacity/role, Insight, Statement, Personality, Experiment — a checklist for structuring rich prompts
An audio compression codec
A new programming language
A type of cookie

items.prompt: What is the 'ReAct' prompting pattern?
options: Reasoning + Acting — the model alternates between thinking aloud and taking tool actions
Reactionary AI behavior
Reading + acting on emails
A React.js framework feature

items.prompt: What does the 'Tree of Thoughts' (ToT) pattern do?
options: Trains on tree datasets
Generates an actual binary tree image
Replaces all model output with tree diagrams
Explores multiple reasoning paths in parallel and picks the best, rather than following one chain

items.prompt: What is the 'rephrase and respond' (RaR) prompt pattern?
options: Send the same question twice and average
Translate the question into another language first
Have the user repeat the question aloud
Ask the model to first rephrase the question in its own words, then answer it

items.prompt: What is the BEST way to learn prompt patterns deeply?
options: Only read tweets about them
Memorize them without testing
Read the original research papers, then test the patterns on your own tasks and measure results
Avoid them entirely

items.prompt: In production, where should your prompts LIVE?
options: In a Google Doc that anyone can edit
Only in your head
Hardcoded as string literals scattered through the codebase
In version-controlled files (or a prompt management service), separate from but tracked with your code

items.prompt: What does 'prompt drift' refer to?
options: When an LLM provider silently updates the underlying model, causing your previously-working prompts to behave differently
When users change their prompts
When prompts physically move on disk
When prompts change language by themselves

items.prompt: Which is a SMART production practice for handling LLM errors?
options: Show the raw stack trace to the user
Retry with exponential backoff, fallback to a cheaper model, and gracefully degrade if all retries fail
Crash the whole application
Silently swallow the error and return nothing

items.prompt: When should you ALWAYS have a human-in-the-loop with LLM output?
options: Never — LLMs are always reliable
Only on weekdays
For every single API call without exception
When the output drives high-stakes actions: legal, medical, financial, irreversible operations

items.prompt: What's the value of LOGGING all prompts and responses in production?
options: Making the app slower
Showing off log size to investors
Debugging failures, building eval sets from real traffic, detecting abuse, and measuring quality over time
Filling up the database for fun

items.prompt: What are 'AI agents' (agentic AI)?
options: AI versions of CIA operatives
Systems where LLMs autonomously plan, use tools, and take multi-step actions to achieve a goal
Email clients for AI
Human salespeople for AI products

items.prompt: What is 'meta-prompting'?
options: Posting prompts on Meta (Facebook)
Prompts about prompts in philosophy
Using an LLM to generate or improve prompts for itself or another LLM
Encrypting prompts with meta-keys

items.prompt: What is 'fine-tuning' and how does it differ from prompting?
options: Fine-tuning is exactly the same as prompting
Fine-tuning permanently adjusts model weights on custom data; prompting just changes the input
Fine-tuning makes the model smaller
Fine-tuning is illegal

items.prompt: Why is prompt engineering NOT going away even as models get smarter?
options: Models will never improve
Humans cannot type
Better models still need clear instructions, structured inputs, and well-defined tasks to perform optimally
Prompts will be banned by law

items.prompt: What's the BEST mindset for a long-term prompt engineering career?
options: Avoid all new tools and patterns
Treat it like both an engineering discipline (test, measure, version) and a communication skill (clarity, precision, empathy)
Memorize one perfect prompt and use it forever
Refuse to evaluate outputs
